summary_oneline: Give the FEAT-581 e2e-ui-tester exploration flow a Playwright-backed .webm screencast as an operational log, alongside its existing on-anomaly screenshot.

localization.role: spawns the `obscura serve` CDP endpoint the screencast's Playwright client would connect to; never touches Playwright itself
the agent that would gain the screencast capability; today only takes a one-off screenshot via an optional DevTools MCP tool
existing config surface that already supports CDP-attach video recording
the exact branch that decides whether record_video_dir engages (fresh context) or is silently ignored (reused context)
defines the real artifacts/logs/e2e/<run-id>/<target-id>.log convention a sibling .webm would follow
confirms artifacts/logs/e2e/ is excluded from the deterministic source-identity hash and from the current evidence schema
shows video/screencast was never added to the verified-capability matrix for real Obscura

constraints.statement: record_video_dir only engages in engine="obscura" mode when the CDP endpoint has zero pre-existing browser contexts at connect time; otherwise it is silently ignored.
constraints.implication: the implementation must either force a fresh context or verify (not assume) that the target `obscura serve` process it connects to has none — the `browser` target's `minimal`/owned profile (fresh process per run) is favorable but unverified at runtime.

constraints.statement: No test or doc has verified Playwright's video capture against a real Obscura v0.2.2 binary; it is absent from the compatibility matrix and a sibling CDP feature already has known renderer gaps.
constraints.implication: implementation should follow the repo's existing opt-in real-binary verification pattern (skip cleanly without the binary, never fail the suite) before the capability is trusted.

constraints.statement: artifacts/logs/e2e/ is excluded from the deterministic gate's source-identity hash and is not part of the current E2EVerdict evidence schema.
constraints.implication: the screencast must stay confined to the exploration report (e2e-exploration.json evidence_refs); wiring it into deterministic gate evidence is explicitly out of scope for this proposal.

constraints.statement: artifacts/ is gitignored but has no retention, rotation, or size-cap policy anywhere in the repo.
constraints.implication: an always-on recording policy needs an explicit retention decision (U3); video is far larger than today's screenshots/logs.

new.item: Screencast recording path in the e2e-ui-tester exploration flow: connect a `PlaywrightDriver(PlaywrightConfig(engine="obscura", cdp_endpoint_url=<browser target's ready() endpoint>, record_video_dir=<artifacts/logs/e2e/<run-id>/>))` session instead of (or alongside) the generic DevTools-MCP attach, so the context Playwright creates carries the video option.
A `screencast_ref` entry (or reuse of the existing `evidence_refs` array) in e2e-exploration.json pointing at the recorded `.webm`.

An opt-in, real-Obscura-binary verification test following the existing `test_fixture_site_integration.py` pattern (skip cleanly without a real binary), proving record_video_dir actually produces a playable .webm over a live Obscura CDP endpoint.

modified.change: add the screencast step and the new evidence_refs entry; keep the existing on-anomaly screenshot step unchanged alongside it.

untouched: parrot.e2e.runner / parrot.e2e.models.E2EVerdict — the deterministic gate's evidence schema and source-identity hash stay exactly as they are (F006); no video field is added there.
parrot.e2e.targets.browser._BrowserAdapter — keeps only spawning obscura serve and handing back a CDP endpoint; it never becomes Playwright-aware itself (F001).
e2e-api-tester — no browser surface, out of scope.
the `ui` target's own HTTP-only readiness check.

patterns_to_follow.pattern: opt-in real-binary verification that skips cleanly without the dependency, never fails the suite
artifacts/logs/e2e/<run-id>/<target-id>-shaped file placement, sibling to the existing screenshot path

integration_risks.risk: Obscura v0.2.2 may not support whatever CDP mechanism Playwright's video recording relies on internally, producing a silently empty/missing .webm.
integration_risks.impact: the feature would look implemented but produce no usable evidence, misleading anyone reviewing an exploration run.
integration_risks.mitigation: gate the feature behind the opt-in real-binary spike test (F007) before enabling it by default.

integration_risks.risk: A reused CDP context (not the fresh-context case F001 expects for the `minimal` profile) silently drops the recording.
integration_risks.impact: same as above — no error, just no video.
integration_risks.mitigation: assert/log context freshness at connect time, and fail loud (not silently) rather than recording nothing unnoticed.

integration_risks.risk: Unbounded disk growth in artifacts/logs/e2e/ under always-on recording.
integration_risks.impact: dev-machine or CI-runner disk pressure over repeated runs.
integration_risks.mitigation: decide always-on vs on-anomaly-only (U2) and whether retention is in scope (U3).

confidence_map.statement: The `browser` e2e target only spawns `obscura serve`/exposes a raw CDP endpoint; it never touches Playwright itself.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct read of browser.py's docstring and argv construction.

confidence_map.statement: `e2e-ui-tester` today only captures a one-off PNG screenshot via an optional DevTools MCP tool, not a continuous recording.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct read of the agent definition's tools list and protocol text.

confidence_map.statement: `PlaywrightConfig` already has `record_video_dir` and an `engine="obscura"` CDP-attach mode.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct read of the dataclass fields.

confidence_map.statement: `record_video_dir` only takes effect in Obscura/CDP mode when the endpoint has zero pre-existing browser contexts at connect time; it is silently ignored when an existing context is reused.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct read of PlaywrightDriver._start_obscura_cdp's branching logic, not inferred from the task doc alone.

confidence_map.statement: The `browser` target's `minimal`/owned profile spawns a fresh, isolated obscura process per run, which is the condition favorable to C4's fresh-context branch.
confidence_map.reasoning: combines two findings by inference; no runtime observation confirms the connecting Playwright client actually sees zero contexts in practice.

confidence_map.statement: artifacts/logs/e2e/<run-id>/<target-id>.log is the real per-run log convention, distinct from the private sdd/state/e2e/<run-id>/ run directory.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct read of both path-building functions.

confidence_map.statement: artifacts/logs/e2e/ is already excluded from the deterministic gate's source-identity hash, so writing a video file there is safe and cannot trigger a spurious FAIL.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct quote from the spec's evidence-identity exclusion list.

confidence_map.statement: The deterministic evidence schema (E2EVerdict) does not currently include video as an evidence type.
confidence_map.reasoning: direct quote enumerating the evidence types the spec names.

confidence_map.statement: No existing test or doc has verified that a real Obscura v0.2.2 binary actually supports Playwright's video-recording mechanism.
confidence_map.reasoning: inferred from the absence of a row in the compatibility matrix plus a sibling CDP feature's known real-binary gap; absence-based, not a direct negative test result.

confidence_map.statement: No retention, rotation, or size-cap policy exists for artifacts/logs/e2e/ anywhere in the repo today.
confidence_map.reasoning: no contradicting mechanism found in any reviewed module (state.py, supervisor.py, cli.py) or the spec.

unknowns.question: Should the implementation be gated behind an opt-in real-Obscura-binary spike (verifying record_video_dir actually produces a usable .webm) before the feature ships, given no existing verification that Obscura supports Playwright's video mechanism?
plausible_answers: yes — make the spike the spec's first task/acceptance gate; if it fails, the feature's design needs to change (e.g. raw CDP frame capture instead of Playwright's video option)
no — trust the CDP-compatibility assumption, build the feature directly, and only add the spike as a follow-up if screencasts turn out empty in practice
unknowns.user_answer: yes — gate as the spec's first task/acceptance gate (opt-in real-Obscura spike, skips cleanly without the binary, following the existing test_fixture_site_integration.py pattern).

unknowns.question: Should the screencast be always-on for every e2e-ui-tester exploration run, or captured only on-anomaly (mirroring today's screenshot trigger)?
plausible_answers: always-on — every run gets a full .webm; simplest, matches the 'operational log' framing of the original ask
on-anomaly-only — start/stop recording around the same console-error/5xx trigger the screenshot already uses, smaller disk footprint
hybrid — always-on for a future deterministic UI scenario (small, bounded number of runs), on-anomaly-only for ad hoc exploration
unknowns.user_answer: hybrid — always-on for a future bounded deterministic UI scenario; on-anomaly-only (matching today's screenshot trigger) for ad hoc e2e-ui-tester exploration.

unknowns.question: Is adding a retention/cleanup mechanism for artifacts/logs/e2e/ in scope for this feature, or should it be documented as a known risk and deferred?
plausible_answers: in scope — add a simple age/size-based cleanup as part of this feature
out of scope — document the risk only; defer to a separate housekeeping feature or manual cleanup, same as today's screenshots/logs
unknowns.user_answer: out of scope — document the disk-growth risk only; defer retention/cleanup to a separate housekeeping feature or manual cleanup, same as today's screenshots/logs.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence (C1-C8, C10) and the change is additive/narrowly scoped to the exploration flow (no deterministic-gate changes); the one real architectural fork (C9/U1 — whether Obscura actually supports video capture) is exactly the kind of risk this codebase already handles by making the real-binary check an opt-in, cleanly-skipping spec task rather than a blocking brainstorm.

meta.notes: overall_confidence held at medium (not high) specifically because of C9/U1: the central technical premise (Obscura + Playwright video capture working together) has never been verified against a real binary anywhere in this repo, and scope confidence cannot exceed that gap per rule 4.
